use_case_name: Define Reference Points and Geometric Areas

evidence_cards.content: The objective is to define EW AOPs (refer to paragraph 4.4.7.1.3) using the J3.7I/J3.7C1/J3.7C2 word sequence as a minimum.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Directly states the high-level goal of defining specific operational points (EW AOPs) which aligns with the use case 'Define Reference Points and Geometric Areas'.

evidence_cards.content: The primary actor (C2 JU) aims to request or report filters for Reference Points (including points, lines, and areas reported in J3.0 messages) using the J7.6 message.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Identifies the specific objective of defining and filtering reference points within the context of the J7.6 message protocol.

evidence_cards.content: A C2 JU or a JU capable of generating and maintaining track numbers may report an AOP based either on organic data, exchange of LOBs, analysis of EW fix data, or a combination of the above.

evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This establishes the prerequisite capabilities (generating/maintaining track numbers) and the available input sources (organic data, LOBs, EW fix data) that must exist before the actor can define an AOP.

evidence_cards.content: The unit originating a J3.7 EW Fix, AOP, or LOB report always retains reporting responsibility.

evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This defines the precondition regarding authority; the actor must be the originating unit to retain the responsibility for the definition being created.

evidence_cards.content: The C2 JU initiates the definition of a reference point by generating the J3.0I Reference Point initial word.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Identifies the specific message (J3.0I) and action that starts the use case for defining reference points.

evidence_cards.content: When defining EW AOPs, the J3.7I/J3.7C1/J3.7C2 word sequence is used as a minimum.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines the specific data content (word sequence) required for the primary action of defining an EW AOP in the main flow.

evidence_cards.content: The same procedures described above are used to define AOPs.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Establishes that the standard definition procedure applies to the generation of the AOP message.

evidence_cards.content: The C2 JU reports the Area of Probability (AOP) using a J3.7I/J3.7C1/J3.7C2 word sequence as a minimum.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This defines the primary interaction step where the actor executes the definition of the geometric area using the specific required message structure.

evidence_cards.content: The C2 JU sets the FIX BRG field in the J3.7I word to value 1 to indicate an AOP report.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This is a critical parameter setting within the main flow that distinguishes this specific type of reference point definition from others (like fixes or LOBs).

evidence_cards.content: The C2 JU includes the time the AOP was valid in the J3.7I word and defines the AOP geometry in the J3.7C2 word.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: These are the specific data population steps required to complete the definition of the reference point within the message sequence.

evidence_cards.content: When the C2 JU requests a REFERENCE POINT (via J3.0I), the system responds with J3.0 lines and areas defined by more than one J3.0 message.

source_locations.location: Table 4.7-4, row 'REFERENCE POINT', column 'RESPONSE MESSAGE(S)' and Note 1

evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This specifies the canonical success scenario for the main flow: after the trigger (J3.0I request), the system’s response is constrained to J3.0 messages only, and only when multiple such messages define the area/line — directly shaping the interaction sequence between actor and system.

evidence_cards.content: The J3.0 message provides the capability to transmit lines such as FEBAs, roads, etc.; areas such as search areas, exercise areas, etc.; and volumes such as corridors, etc., in addition to reporting points.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This describes an alternative successful path for defining geometric areas (lines, areas, volumes) using the J3.0 message instead of the main flow’s focus on EW AOPs via J3.7 sequence — thus qualifying as a legal alternative flow diverging from the canonical point-definition scenario.

evidence_cards.content: The J3.5 message also provides the capability to describe a circle/ellipse about a ground point, which could be used with any J3.5 point (not just SAM sites).
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This represents another valid alternative flow where the actor defines a geometric area (circle/ellipse) around a ground point using J3.5, diverging from the main flow’s use of J3.7 for EW AOPs — still resulting in successful definition of a reference/geometric area.

evidence_cards.content: When defining EW AOPs (refer to paragraph 4.4.7.1.3) the J3.7I/J3.7C1/J3.7C2 word sequence, as a minimum, is used.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This sentence explicitly identifies an alternative flow for defining EW AOPs by specifying a minimum word sequence requirement that diverges from the general geometric area definition procedures described earlier in the document.

evidence_cards.content: When an EW AOP results from previously reported LOBs, it shall be assigned a new TN, not one of the TNs assigned to the LOBs.

evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This is a legal alternative path for defining an EW AOP (reference point) that diverges from the main flow by specifying how Track Numbers are handled when deriving the AOP from prior LOB reports.

evidence_cards.content: When an EW AOP results from two or more previously reported fixes of differing TNs, it shall be assigned a new TN, not one of the TNs assigned to the fixes.

evidence_cards.content: When a fix is changed to an AOP, the TN of the previously reported fix shall be used for the new AOP.

evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This is a legal alternative path that diverges from the main flow by reusing an existing TN instead of assigning a new one when converting a fix to an AOP.

evidence_cards.content: Optionally, alerts may be cleared by reception of a J3.0 message with FT IND set to value 0.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This describes an alternative flow for terminating a force tell alert that diverges from the main flow (which requires transmitting a J7.0 ACT=4 message). It represents a still-successful variant path for clearing alerts without using the primary termination mechanism.

evidence_cards.content: Optionally, alerts may be cleared by reception of a J3.0 message with the FT IND set to value 0.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Reinforces the optional alternative flow for clearing alerts via J3.0 message reception instead of requiring explicit J7.0 ACT=4 transmission, applicable when JU lacks R² capability.

evidence_cards.content: If an EW AOP is formed from a single fix, the same TN shall be retained; if an EW AOP is formed from 2 or more fixes, a new TN shall be assigned.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This defines an exception condition (forming AOP from multiple fixes) that triggers mandatory assignment of a new TN — deviating from the default behavior implied in main flow where TN may be retained. This is a concrete error/exception handling path for track number continuity during entity type change.

evidence_cards.content: For data report type 4 (datum), the same TN may be used by operator action.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This specifies an exception to standard TN assignment rules: under specific data report conditions (type 4 datum), TN reuse is permitted via manual operator intervention — representing an exceptional override path not covered in canonical success scenario.

evidence_cards.content: After successful completion of the use case, the EW AOP is defined and represented in the system using the J3.7I/J3.7C1/J3.7C2 word sequence as a minimum, with all required fields (such as FIX BRG = 1 for AOP, validity time, and geometry) correctly populated per the main flow steps.

evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This describes the observable system state after the C2 JU successfully defines an EW AOP — specifically, that the definition is complete and minimally compliant with the required word sequence, which constitutes the postcondition of the use case.

evidence_cards.content: If the EW AOP is slaved to a Related TN (Slaved Indicator = 1), then its position is established as Delta Latitude, 1/Delta Longitude, 1 from the Related TN at report time, establishing constant true or relative bearing and range — this becomes part of the persistent state if slaving was applied during definition.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This specifies an additional observable postcondition when slaving is used: the spatial relationship between the AOP and the Related TN is fixed at report time and maintained thereafter, affecting how the AOP’s position is interpreted or plotted.

evidence_cards.content: If the proposed EW AOP definition is accepted by the receiving JU, the system state reflects the new entity type: the originating JU transmits a J7.0 (ACT=0) Drop Track message for the original TN and reports the entity as a NEW TN in the appropriate J3.x Surveillance Message or J5.4 Message.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines the specific system state change (new track number assignment and reporting format) that occurs after the successful completion of an Environment/Category change to EW AOP involving multiple fixes.

evidence_cards.content: If the EW AOP definition is formed from a single fix, the system retains the original Track Number (TN), and the entity is reported in the appropriate J3.x Surveillance Message.
